intro: Wisconsin’s Fall 2026–Spring 2027 regulations include clear statewide dates, but deer authorizations, bear units, elk permits, turkey periods and waterfowl zones still matter. Check the current DNR map and regulation for your unit, county and land type before hunting.
zoneNote: Deer rules vary by DMU, Metro Subunit, county and land type; bear dates and dog rules vary by Bear Management Zone; elk is limited to selected residents and units; waterfowl dates differ among Northern, Southern, Open Water and Mississippi River zones.

licenseAndEducation.fact: Purchase licenses, stamps and permits through the official Go Wild portal or an authorized DNR license sales agent. Check Go Wild for unit-specific authorizations and current availability.

Anyone born on or after Jan. 1, 1973 must complete hunter education and have a certificate on file before buying a hunting license, unless using the mentorship program or documented qualifying U.S. military basic training.

For bow hunting, people born on or after Jan. 1, 1973 need hunter education or bowhunter education. Bowhunter-only certification authorizes archery/crossbow licenses only, subject to stated exceptions.

Official fees: small game $18 resident/$90 nonresident; state waterfowl stamp $12; federal stamp $28.50; early/regular goose permit $3; turkey license $15/$65 plus $5.25 wild-turkey stamp; gun deer, archery and crossbow $24/$200; bear application $4.50 and drawn license $49/$251; elk application $10 resident-only and drawn license $49 resident-only. Junior prices and bonus authorizations differ by program.

2026 bonus antlerless authorizations are first-come and subject to availability: $12 resident, $20 nonresident, $5 youth under 12. One to five Farmland authorizations may be included with each deer license depending on unit choice.

The 2026 elk hunt was open only to Wisconsin residents. Selected hunters must complete Wisconsin elk hunter education before obtaining the license. A resident can receive only one elk hunting license in a lifetime.

Waterfowl hunters generally need a small-game license, Wisconsin waterfowl stamp, federal waterfowl stamp, HIP registration and any applicable early or regular goose permit. Hunters age 16+ need both state and federal stamps.
